explore.title: Explore an open pit
explore.lead: A 3D open pit with twelve simulation cases — haulage, blasting, slopes, dust, water, autonomy and more — each computed by the repository's own physics, simulation and learned models.

cases.title: Cases
cases.lead: The case catalogue: what each scenario simulates, which tools produce it, and how its results are checked.

studio.title: Studio
studio.lead: The local GPU studio: which simulation, sensor, synthetic-data, training and acceleration tools run where, and what each one produced.

theory.title: Theory
theory.lead: The physics and mining-engineering models behind every case, with equations, assumptions and primary references.

methods.title: Methods
methods.lead: The method ladder for each task: classical baselines, current state of the art, and learned models, compared on held-out data.

results.title: Results
results.lead: Measured results from committed artifacts: accuracy against baselines, simulation-to-real gaps, and acceleration benchmarks.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.lead: Glossary, equations, parameter tables, datasets, frameworks and bibliography — the knowledge base of the repository.

what.title: What it is
what.body: PitStudio applies physical-AI simulation to open-pit mining. A local GPU studio builds OpenUSD scenes, runs physics and sensor simulation, generates synthetic data and trains models; this site explains the cases and replays or recomputes their results.

lanes.title: Lanes
lanes.body: Live: light computation runs in your browser (WebGPU, then WebAssembly, then a precomputed fallback). Precompute: heavy simulation and training run on a local GPU workstation. Replay: this site animates the committed outputs of those runs.

studio.title: Studio
studio.body: The studio is a set of isolated local environments, one per toolchain (scene authoring and physics, robotics simulation, RTX sensor rendering, reinforcement learning, model acceleration), run by one runner that records GPU telemetry and a manifest for every output.

webflow.title: Web flow
webflow.body: Static site on GitHub Pages. Every route is prerendered HTML. Large assets (3D tiles, videos, ONNX models) load on demand with progress and are verified against the published manifest.

science.title: Science flow
science.body: Download real data → synthesize scenarios → simulate → extract features → train → evaluate on held-out data → export. Every number shown on this site traces back to a manifest of the run that produced it.

contracts.title: Contracts
contracts.body: Every artifact that crosses a boundary (pipeline to web, studio to pipeline) is described by a JSON Schema in the repository's contracts folder; the web app validates what it loads.

tools.title: Tools
tools.body: Open tools are used and cited; proprietary SDKs are installed by the user from their official sources and never redistributed by this repository. Performance figures of licence-restricted tools are not published.
